test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 19 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Metals are electropositive in nature.

Which of the following is the correct explanation for the given assertion?

options.text: Metals gain electrons to form cations.
Metals gain electrons to form anions.
Metals lose electrons to form cations.
Metals lose electrons to form anions.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Metals lose electrons to form cations.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Metals are generally electropositive, meaning they have a tendency to lose electrons during chemical reactions.
 
• When metals lose electrons, they form positively charged ions known as cations.
 
• The process of losing electrons by metals is called oxidation.
 
• Metals such as sodium (Na), potassium (K), and calcium (Ca) readily lose electrons to form cations like Na⁺, K⁺, and Ca²⁺ respectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electropositivity**

 
 
• Electropositivity refers to the tendency of an atom to donate electrons and form positive ions (cations).
 
• It is the opposite of electronegativity, which is the tendency to attract electrons.
 
• In the periodic table, electropositivity increases as we move down a group and decreases across a period from left to right.
 
 
 
• **Cations**
 
 
• A cation is a positively charged ion that is formed when an atom loses one or more electrons.
 
• Cations are typically formed by metals.
 
• The formation of cations leads to a decrease in the atomic radius due to the loss of electron(s).
 
 
 
• **Oxidation**
 
 
• Oxidation is the process in which an atom loses electrons, resulting in an increase in its oxidation state.
 
• In the context of metals, oxidation involves the loss of electrons to form cations.
 
• The term 'oxidation' originally referred to reactions involving oxygen, but it has been broadened to include all processes involving the loss of electrons.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Cation Formation**
 
 
• Sodium (Na) loses one electron to form Na⁺.
 
• Calcium (Ca) loses two electrons to form Ca²⁺.
 
• Aluminum (Al) loses three electrons to form Al³⁺.
